content.title: Why Should I Be the One to Apologize First?
content.subtitle: The ego that stands in the way of our good deeds and inner peace!
content.body:
Life is strange. In this temporary world, we build so many invisible walls around ourselves! Over a small argument, a trivial misunderstanding, or a minor conflict of interest, we stop talking to our own siblings, relatives, and friends for years. Even while living under the same roof and breathing the same air, we become complete strangers to one another. A heavy burden settles in everyone's heart: “They were also at fault. Why should I take the first step? Why should I humble myself?”

When Ego Becomes a Silent Killer

This “I” or ego, silently destroys our family bonds and inner peace. We think that by turning away or remaining silent, we are punishing the other person. But have we ever considered how much we are actually depriving ourselves in the process? The poison of anger and resentment steals our sleep and leaves us with constant restlessness. Yet, a little humility could have transformed the entire situation into one of peace and harmony.

Is Your Record of Deeds Being Held Back?

We pray, fast, and shed tears during Tahajjud. But are our acts of worship truly being accepted by Allah? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us a serious warning. He said:

“On Mondays and Thursdays, the deeds of people are presented to Allah. Everyone who does not associate partners with Allah is forgiven, except two people who have enmity between them. It is said: Leave these two until they reconcile with one another.” (Sahih Muslim: 2565)

The Prophet ﷺ also said: “The person who severs ties of kinship will not enter Paradise.” (Sahih al-Bukhari: 5984)

Just think about it. Because of a little ego, our hard-earned deeds may be held back from receiving Allah's forgiveness!

An Extraordinary Example of Forgiveness from History

Forgiving someone or taking the first step is not a sign of weakness; it is true courage. Look at the life of our beloved Prophet's ﷺ closest companion, Abu Bakr (RA). During the return journey from the expedition of Banu Mustaliq, Ummul Mu'minin Aisha (RA) was accidentally left behind by the caravan. Taking advantage of this opportunity, the hypocrites spread a terrible false accusation against her, known as the Incident of Ifk.

Painfully, one of Abu Bakr's (RA) poor relatives, Mistah (RA), also became involved in spreading the accusation, even though Abu Bakr (RA) was financially supporting him. Deeply hurt, Abu Bakr (RA) vowed never to help him again. Then Allah revealed verse 22 of Surah An-Nur: “Would you not love that Allah should forgive you?”

Upon hearing this verse, Abu Bakr (RA) said with tears in his eyes, “Yes, by Allah! I certainly wish that Allah should forgive me.” He immediately forgave Mistah (RA) and resumed supporting him.

Let the First Step Toward Reconciliation Begin With You

A Hadith tells us that when two people become estranged, the one who initiates the greeting or conversation first is better in the sight of Allah. (Sahih al-Bukhari: 6077)

In the Holy Quran, Allah describes the true believers as those who restrain their anger and forgive others. And Allah loves those who do good. (Surah Aal-Imran: 134)

Imagine receiving the news tomorrow that someone you love has passed away. The words left unspoken and the burden of resentment may haunt you for the rest of your life.

So why wait any longer? Break down that wall of ego today. Pick up your phone, send a simple message, or make a call and say, “Assalamu Alaikum, how are you?” In Sha Allah, that one small step from you may bring back the peace you have been missing.
